record.paper_title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}}
record.context_brief: Higher-period cycles for the general delayed family in Eq. (19).
record.original_question: Consider the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,2,\ldots. Can this equation have periodic cycles whose prime period is greater than two?

evidence.quote: Open problem 2. (c) Do there exist periodic cycles of period greater than two?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A>0$, $p>0$ be real parameters and $k\ge 1$ an integer. Consider the delay difference equation
$$x_{n+1}=\frac{A}{x_n^{2}}+\frac{1}{x_{n-k}^{\,p}},\qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots,$$
with positive initial conditions $x_{-k},x_{-k+1},\ldots,x_{-1},x_0>0$ (so that all iterates remain positive and well-defined). A solution $(x_n)_{n\ge -k}$ is called periodic with prime period $T\ge 1$ if $x_{n+T}=x_n$ for all $n\ge -k$ and $T$ is the smallest such positive integer.

Determine whether there exist choices of the parameters $A>0$, $p>0$, the delay $k\ge 1$, and positive initial conditions for which the equation admits a periodic solution of prime period strictly greater than $2$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any publication that resolves the existence of prime-period-greater-than-two cycles for this specific family of rational delay difference equations. Related literature treats analogous equations (e.g., $x_{n+1}=A+B x_{n-m}/x_n^2$) and general periodic-structure questions, but no decisive result for the stated equation was found.

status_evidence.title: On the Periodic Structure of Delayed Difference Equations of the Form x_n=f(x_{n-k})
status_evidence.snippet: Combinatorial classification of periodic solutions of delayed difference equations x_n=f(x_{n-k}).
status_evidence.claim: General framework exists but does not address the specific two-term rational equation in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Some Notes on the Difference Equation x_{n+1}=alpha + x_{n-1}/x_n^k
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodicity and stability for related rational delay equations.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct equation; does not resolve the higher-period question for the equation in the problem.
